title: fix(jest-source-map): resolve absolute Windows paths in `sources`
body:
## Summary

Fixes #16438.

Since #16327, `@jest/source-map` hands a map to `@jridgewell/trace-mapping` with the generated file's `file:` URL as the base, and the tracer resolves `sources` as URLs. Its resolver only treats a string as absolute when it starts with `/` or has `scheme://`, so a Windows drive path like `C:/repro/repro.test.js` counts as relative and is appended to the base directory. Mapped frames then show `C:\repro\C:\repro\repro.test.js`.

ts-jest emits absolute, slash-normalized `sources`, so every Windows user of it hit this in 30.5.x. babel-jest emits a bare basename, which is why the default setup was unaffected.

`SourceMapCache` now converts drive paths in `sources` and `sourceRoot` to `file:` URLs through the reader's `toUrl` before parsing, including inside sectioned maps. `source-map-support` did the same job with `path.resolve`.

UNC paths (`\\server\share\…`) fall through the same resolver and are not handled here.

## Test plan

Unit tests use a fake reader so the Windows case runs deterministically on every OS. They fail on `main` and pass with the fix:

```
Tests:       3 failed, 30 passed, 33 total   # main
Tests:       57 passed, 57 total             # this branch, yarn jest packages/jest-source-map
```

The reporter's [repro](https://github.com/mceachen/jest-windows-sourcemap-repro) only fails on Windows, so the Windows CI lane is the end-to-end check.
